title: Motor Imagery ataset from Ofner et al 2017
description: EEG recordings from fifteen healthy participants who executed and imagined six sustained upper limb movements (elbow flexion/extension, forearm supination/pronation, hand open/close) plus a rest condition, in two separate sessions. The dataset supports decoding of single upper limb movements from the time-domain of low-frequency EEG. It is relevant to non-invasive control of motor neuroprostheses and robotic arms. This BIDS version was generated from the original BNCI Horizon 2020 data using MOABB.
methods_description: 61-channel EEG (plus EOG) was recorded at 512 Hz with g.tec active electrodes, referenced to the right mastoid with ground at AFz. Online filtering was 0.01-200 Hz bandpass with a 50 Hz notch. Participants completed 10 runs per session of cued trials in movement execution and motor imagery sessions. The original study filtered to 0.3-3 Hz and classified with shrinkage LDA using discriminative spatial patterns.
